en: The Verses for Auspiciousness:
Homage be to the Buddha; homage be to Awakening;
homage to Liberation; homage to Deliverance.
Homage be to knowledge; homage be to the possessor of knowledge;
pay homage to the one who is most excellent in the highest world! ||1||
Whatever beings have gathered here, whether they belong to the earth or to the atmosphere—
may they all become joyful in heart.
May they hear this auspicious prayer spoken by the Jina. ||2||
Whatever exquisite jewel there may be in this world, or again in the next, or in the heavens,
none is equal to the Tathāgata.
By this truth that the Supreme among Men, the God beyond gods,
has proclaimed this jewel of the Buddha—
by this truth, may there be well-being.
Whether from a human or from a non-human. ||3||
[That which Śākyamuni, being in meditative equipoise, attained— destruction, dispassion, the deathless, the sublime— there is nothing whatsoever equal to that Dharma.]
This too is the sublime jewel of the Dharma.
By this truth, may there be well-being from humans or from non-humans. ||4||
That pure concentration which the Best of Buddhas has praised,
which they call the "uninterrupted" (ānantarya) concentration—
there is nothing equal to that concentration.
This too is a sublime jewel of the Dharma;
by this truth, may there be well-being from humans or from non-humans. ||5||
Those eight persons who are always praised, consisting of these four pairs—
they have been declared by the Sugata to be worthy of offerings.
These gifts bestowed yield great fruit;
this jewel is also most excellent within the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Whether from a human or from a non-human being. ||6||
For one who possesses the excellence of vision,
three qualities are abandoned:
the view of a self-identity and doubt.
And whatever morality and vows there may be—
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha;
by this truth, may there be well-being.
Whether from humans or from non-humans. ||7||
Even if a trainee should commit an evil deed by body, speech, or even by mind,
he is incapable of concealing it.
Incapacity regarding the noble paths has been declared;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Whether from humans or from non-humans. ||8||
Just as a central pillar fixed in the earth would be unshaken by the four winds,
even so do I describe a true person.
Whoever, having approached, beholds the well-taught Noble Truths of profound meaning—
this too is a sublime treasure within the Saṃgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being from humans or from non-humans. ||9||
Those who contemplate the Noble Truths well-taught by one of profound wisdom— even if they should become greatly negligent— will [not fall].
Your honors do not cling to the eight [worldly conditions].
This too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha;
by this truth, may there be well-being.
Whether from a human or from a non-human. ||10||
Those practitioners who are disciplined in yoga with a well-directed mind, seeking renunciation within the teaching of Gautama—
they have attained what was to be attained, having plunged into the deathless.
With minds liberated, enjoying Nirvana—
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha;
by this truth, may there be great well-being.
Whether from humans or from non-humans. ||11||
The old is exhausted and there is no accumulation of the new;
they are liberated from future existence, their seeds destroyed, subject to the nature of non-renewal.
The wise go out like oil lamps;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Whether from a human or from a non-human. ||12||
Just as a blazing fire that has arisen with great force subsides upon the exhaustion of its fuel,
so do the sons of the Buddha who practice such meditation.
Having grasped the latent tendency of passion through wisdom, they go beyond the sight of the King of Death;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
Whether from humans or from non-humans. ||13||
In the first month of summer, Caitra,
the forest thickets with their flowering tops waft a fragrant scent when stirred by the wind.
The sons of the Buddha who meditate in such a way, endowed with virtue, waft a fragrant scent;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being from humans or from non-humans. ||14||
Whatever beings have gathered here, whether they dwell upon the earth or in the atmosphere,
may they always treat human beings with loving-kindness.
Day and night they carry away your tribute;
therefore, protect it with vigilance,
just as a mother protects her son out of compassion.
By this truth, may there be well-being from humans or from non-humans. ||15||
In Vipaśyin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Bhāmaka, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa of great power, and Śākyamuni Gautama;
May those deities who have placed their faith in these Buddhas of great supernatural power protect you thoroughly and grant you their favor.
It is for the well-being of human beings;
therefore, protect it with vigilance,
just as a mother protects her son out of compassion.
[This too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being from humans or from non-humans. ||16||
He who, having overcome the world, sets in motion the Wheel of Dharma that causes all beings to tremble—
such is the one supreme among gods and humans.
I pay homage to the Buddha; may there be well-being.
I pay homage to the Dharma; may there be well-being. I pay homage to the Saṅgha; may there be well-being.
Whether from a human or from a non-human. ||17||
[Thus ends the verse for auspiciousness.]
